Assume the scalar model adoption planned in [[post-qft-free-field-model]] and Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]]. Let $\mu\ge0$ and use the model, shell, field, vacuum, and units of [[def-qft-free-scalar-model]] and [[def-qft-scalar-mass-shell]]. These are conditional model deductions, with no empirical premise. For every Schwartz test $f$, $\Phi_\mu(f)$ is defined on $\mathcal D_{\mathrm{fin}}$; for real $f$ it is symmetric and essentially self-adjoint there. Distributionally, $\Phi_\mu((\Box-\mu^2)f)=0$. The Fock lift of the proper orthochronous Poincare action is unitary, leaves $\Omega$ invariant, and implements covariance of the smeared field. For real Schwartz tests the vacuum two-point form is $\langle\Omega,\Phi_\mu(f)\Phi_\mu(g)\Omega\rangle=\langle K_\mu f,K_\mu g\rangle_2$, and it is nonnegative when $g=f$. The joint spectrum of spacetime translations is contained in the closed forward cone. For real compactly supported smooth tests with pairwise spacelike-separated supports, the smeared fields commute on $\mathcal D_{\mathrm{fin}}$. The bounded local Weyl algebras are isotonic and algebras for spacelike-separated regions commute. The physical Hamiltonian is self-adjoint on the exact multiplier domain in [[def-qft-free-scalar-model]], is nonnegative, and has $\Omega$ as its unique zero-energy vector. If $\mu>0$, the infimum of its positive spectrum is $\hbar c\mu=m_{\mathrm{rest,SI}}c^2$. If $\mu=0$, its positive spectrum has no gap above zero.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $n \ge 1$, let $S^{n-1} \subseteq \mathbb R^n$ be the unit sphere, and let $\sigma$ be the set function of [[def-polar-surface-measure-on-the-unit-sphere]]. Then $\sigma$ is a finite Borel measure on $S^{n-1}$, and for every Borel measurable $f : \mathbb R^n \to [0,\infty]$, $$\int_{\mathbb R^n} f(x)\,d\lambda_n(x) = \int_0^\infty \int_{S^{n-1}} f(r\omega) r^{n-1}\,d\sigma(\omega)\,dr.$$ Moreover, $\sigma$ is the unique Borel measure on $S^{n-1}$ with this property.

Let $n \ge 1$, **assume the Axiom of Countable Choice** ([[def-countable-choice]]) and let $T : \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}^n$ be linear with matrix $A$ ([[def-linear-map]], [[lem-euclidean-linear-maps-have-matrices-and-are-bounded]]). 1. **Invertible case.** If $\det A \ne 0$, then $T[E]$ is Lebesgue measurable for every Lebesgue measurable $E$ and $$\lambda_n\big(T[E]\big) \;=\; |\det A|\;\lambda_n(E),$$ both sides possibly $+\infty$; the product is defined in $\overline{\mathbb{R}}$ because $|\det A| > 0$. 2. **Singular case.** If $\det A = 0$, then $T[E]$ is Lebesgue measurable with $\lambda_n(T[E]) = 0$ for **every** $E \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$. **The singular clause is stated as nullity and not as a product.** When $\det A = 0$ and $\lambda_n(E) = +\infty$ the expression $|\det A|\,\lambda_n(E)$ is $0\cdot(+\infty)$, which [[def-extended-reals]] leaves undefined; writing the conclusion as $\lambda_n(T[E]) = 0$ says the same thing wherever the product is defined and remains a statement where it is not.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Fix $n \ge 1$ and write $$S^{n-1}:=\{\omega \in \mathbb R^n : |\omega|=1\}.$$ Let $$\Phi:\mathbb R^n\setminus\{0\}\longrightarrow(0,\infty)\times S^{n-1},\qquad \Phi(x)=(|x|,x/|x|).$$ This map is continuous. If $E\subseteq S^{n-1}$ is Borel, then $(0,1]\times E$ is Borel and $$\{r\omega:\omega\in E,\ 0<r\le1\}=\Phi^{-1}((0,1]\times E)$$ is Borel in $\mathbb R^n\setminus\{0\}$ by [[thm-continuous-preimages-of-borel-sets-are-borel]], hence Borel in $\mathbb R^n$ by [[thm-borel-sigma-algebra-of-a-subspace-is-the-trace]]. It is therefore Lebesgue measurable by [[thm-borel-sets-are-lebesgue-measurable]]. Define $$\sigma(E):=n\,\lambda_n(\{r\omega : \omega \in E,\ 0<r\le 1\}).$$ The next theorem proves that this is a Borel measure on $S^{n-1}$ and that it is exactly the surface measure needed for polar coordinates.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $S^2:=\{x\in\mathbb R^3:|x|=1\}$ and let $\sigma$ be the polar surface measure on $S^2$ of [[def-polar-surface-measure-on-the-unit-sphere]], a finite Borel measure ([[def-measure]], [[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]). Let $$\Phi:(0,\pi)\times(0,2\pi)\to S^2,\qquad \Phi(\theta,\varphi):=(\sin\theta\cos\varphi,\ \sin\theta\sin\varphi,\ \cos\theta),$$ and let $H:=\{(x,y,0)\in\mathbb R^3:x\ge0\}$ denote the closed half-plane, a Lebesgue-null Borel set ([[thm-affine-hyperplanes-and-proper-subspaces-of-rn-are-lebesgue-null]]). Then: (a) for every Borel function $F:S^2\to[0,+\infty]$, $$\int_{S^2}F\,d\sigma=\int_{(0,\pi)\times(0,2\pi)}F\bigl(\Phi(\theta,\varphi)\bigr)\,\sin\theta\ d(\theta,\varphi),$$ the right-hand integral being the Lebesgue integral over the open rectangle; (b) $\sigma(S^2)=4\pi$; (c) the identity of (a) holds with $F\in L^1(S^2,\sigma;\mathbb C)$ in the sense that $F\circ\Phi$ is Lebesgue integrable on the rectangle against $\sin\theta\,d(\theta,\varphi)$ and the two integrals agree (real and imaginary parts, positive and negative parts).

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]], let $\mu\ge0$, let
$H_\mu$ and $K_\mu$ be as in [[def-qft-scalar-mass-shell]], and form
$\mathcal F_s(H_\mu)$ with vacuum $\Omega$ and finite-particle domain
$\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$. For $f\in\mathscr S(\mathbb R^4)$ define on
$\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$
$$\Phi_\mu(f)=a(K_\mu\overline f)+a^\dagger(K_\mu f).$$
This is a complex-linear map of test functions into operators
$\mathcal D_{\rm fin}\to\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$. For real $f$ it is symmetric
and equals $\sqrt2\,\Phi_{\rm Segal}(K_\mu f)|_{\mathcal D_{\rm fin}}$, where the Segal field of
[[lem-qft-segal-weyl-domain]] is
$\Phi_{\rm Segal}(h)=\overline{(a^\dagger(h)+a(h))/\sqrt2}$.
Thus its Weyl unitary is
$W_\mu(f):=W_{\rm Segal}(\sqrt2 K_\mu f)$ and, for real $f,g$,
$$W_\mu(f)W_\mu(g)= e^{-i\,\operatorname{Im}\langle K_\mu f,K_\mu g\rangle_2}W_\mu(f+g).$$
For every real $f$ the vacuum Weyl expectation is
$$\langle\Omega,W_\mu(f)\Omega\rangle_2 =e^{-\|K_\mu f\|_2^2/2}.$$
Here the inner product is second-variable-linear as fixed in
[[def-qft-fock-and-test-spaces]]. The vacuum has zero one-point function and
two-point function
$$\langle\Omega,\Phi_\mu(f)\Phi_\mu(g)\Omega\rangle_2 =\langle K_\mu\overline f,K_\mu g\rangle_2,$$
which obeys $\langle\Omega,\Phi_\mu(\overline f)\Phi_\mu(f)\Omega\rangle_2=\|K_\mu f\|_2^2\ge0$ for every complex test $f$ (ordinary diagonal positivity holds for real tests); higher vacuum moments of ordered real smeared
fields obey the CCR pairing recursion and hence the free-field Wick pairing
rule. The field is a weak operator-valued tempered distribution on $\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$: every matrix coefficient $f\mapsto\langle\Psi,\Phi_\mu(f)\Theta\rangle_2$ for $\Psi,\Theta\in\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$ is a continuous complex-linear functional on Schwartz space. Its adjoint satisfies $\Phi_\mu(f)^*|_{\mathcal D_{\rm fin}}=\Phi_\mu(\overline f)$, and its normalized vacuum defines a positive state on the finite polynomial $*$-algebra generated by these fields.

The relative-coordinate two-point tempered distribution is
$$W_\mu(z)=\int_{H_\mu^+}e^{-ip\circ z}\,d\nu_\mu(p),$$
understood by pairing with Schwartz tests. Its translation-invariant bidistribution is the shell integral of $e^{-ip\circ x}e^{ip\circ y}$; on product tests it is the displayed vacuum covariance.

For $g=(a,\Lambda)$, let $f_g$ and $U_\mu(g)$ be the affine test pullback
and one-particle action of [[lem-qft-scalar-poincare-action]]. Their Fock
lifts implement the same covariance for $\Phi_\mu$ on $\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$
and for the bounded Weyl operators.

For translations, the joint spectral measure on Fock space is the
second-quantized multiplier measure with one-particle vector
$(\omega_\mu(\mathbf k),-\mathbf k)$. Its support is contained in the closed
future cone $\{(E,\mathbf P):E\ge|\mathbf P|\}$; the vacuum is an eigenvector
at $(0,\mathbf0)$. These are conditional mathematical model deductions.
No point field, empirical observation or measurement claim is made.

Assume Countable Choice. For $\mu\ge0$, define the tempered distribution
$$\Delta_\mu(t,\mathbf x)= \int_{\mathbb R^3}\frac{d^3\mathbf k}{(2\pi)^3} \frac{\sin(\omega_\mu(\mathbf k)t)}{\omega_\mu(\mathbf k)} e^{i\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf x},$$
with the massless integrand defined off $\mathbf k=0$; its $1/|\mathbf k|$
behavior is locally integrable in three dimensions. Then
$$\operatorname{supp}\Delta_\mu \subseteq\{(t,\mathbf x):t^2-|\mathbf x|^2\ge0\},$$
the closed causal cone for the $(-+++)$ metric. For real compactly supported
smooth $f,g$, put
$$\Delta_\mu(f,g)= \int_{\mathbb R^4}\!\int_{\mathbb R^4} f(x)g(y)\Delta_\mu(x-y)\,d^4x\,d^4y.$$
On $\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$ the smeared fields of
[[lem-qft-smeared-free-scalar]] satisfy
$$[\Phi_\mu(f),\Phi_\mu(g)]=-i\Delta_\mu(f,g)I.$$
Consequently spacelike-separated supports give commuting fields.

Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]].
Let $O\subseteq\mathbb R^4$ be open. For real
$f\in C_c^\infty(O)$ define
$$W_\mu(f):=W_{\rm Segal}(\sqrt2K_\mu f),$$
where the Segal normalization is exactly
$\Phi_{\rm Segal}(h)=(a^\dagger(h)+a(h))/\sqrt2$ on the finite-particle
domain, as in [[lem-qft-segal-weyl-domain]]. This scale makes the generator
of $t\mapsto W_\mu(tf)$ equal to the real scalar field
$\Phi_\mu(f)=a(K_\mu f)+a^\dagger(K_\mu f)$ of
[[lem-qft-smeared-free-scalar]]. Define the unital norm-closed operator
algebra
$$\mathfrak A_\mu(O)= \overline{\operatorname{alg}}^{\|\cdot\|} \{I,W_\mu(f),W_\mu(f)^*:f\in C_c^\infty(O;\mathbb R)\}.$$
Then $O_1\subseteq O_2$ implies
$\mathfrak A_\mu(O_1)\subseteq\mathfrak A_\mu(O_2)$. If every difference
$x-y$, with $x\in O_1$ and $y\in O_2$, is spacelike, then every element of
$\mathfrak A_\mu(O_1)$ commutes with every element of
$\mathfrak A_\mu(O_2)$. These are algebraic properties of the constructed
representation; they are not empirical signaling or measurement claims.

If $\widehat f(\xi^0,\boldsymbol\xi)=

Its inverse is

Let $f$ and $(f_n)$ be measurable complex-valued functions such that
$f_n\to f$ almost everywhere and $|f_n|\le g$ almost everywhere for a single

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ and $(Y,\mathcal B,\nu)$ be sigma-finite measure
spaces, and let $f : X \times Y \to \mathbb C$ belong to
$L^1(\mu \times \nu)$. Then:

1. for $\mu$-almost every $x$, the section $f_x$ belongs to $L^1(\nu)$;

$$|\langle x,y\rangle|\le\|x\|\,\|y\| ,$$

with equality if and only if $x$ and $y$ are linearly dependent.

derivations.claim:
Choose $\delta>0$. By [F4], choose a nonnegative nonzero
$\chi\in C_c^\infty((-\delta,\delta))$. Choose two nonnegative nonzero
$u,v\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$ supported in closed balls of radii
$r_1,r_2$ whose center separation $D$ satisfies
$D-r_1-r_2>2\delta$. Such bumps follow by translating and rescaling [F4].
Set $f(t,\mathbf x)=\chi(t)u(\mathbf x)$ and
$g(t,\mathbf x)=\chi(t)v(\mathbf x)$. For every point in the two supports,
$|t-s|<2\delta$ and $|\mathbf x-\mathbf y|\ge D-r_1-r_2>2\delta$;
therefore all support differences are spacelike.
For example, $\delta=1$, $r_1=r_2=1$ and $D=5$ give a spatial gap of $3>2$,
so these strict inequalities are attainable.

Insert a radial regulator $e^{-\epsilon|\mathbf k|}$, $\epsilon>0$, in
the massless two-point kernel. Angular integration using [F3] gives for
$r=|\mathbf x-\mathbf y|>0$ and $\tau=t-s$
$$W_\epsilon(\tau,r)=
\frac{1}{4\pi^2r}\int_0^\infty
e^{-(\epsilon+i\tau)q}\sin(qr)\,dq
=\frac{1}{4\pi^2\bigl(r^2+(\epsilon+i\tau)^2\bigr)}.$$
The integral identity follows by integrating the two exponentials in the
sine and using $\operatorname{Re}(\epsilon+i\tau)>0$. On the compact
support product in 1.1, $r\ge d:=D-r_1-r_2>2\delta>|\tau|$. Thus the
denominator is bounded away from zero uniformly as $\epsilon\downarrow0$,
and $W_\epsilon$ converges uniformly there to
$[4\pi^2(r^2-\tau^2)]^{-1}$, which is strictly positive.

The regulated shell integrals converge to
$\langle K_0 f,K_0 g\rangle_2$ by dominated convergence [F5]: the absolute
value of the unregulated product is integrable by Cauchy–Schwarz [F7],
because $K_0f,K_0g\in H_0$. To identify the regulated shell integral with
the spacetime pairing of $W_\epsilon$, Fubini [F6] applies because its
absolute integral is at most
$\|f\|_1\|g\|_1\int_{\mathbb R^3}e^{-\epsilon|\mathbf k|}
d^3\mathbf k/[(2\pi)^3 2|\mathbf k|]<\infty$.
The formula in 2.1 and uniform convergence on the compact support product give
$$\langle K_0 f,K_0 g\rangle_2
=\int f(t,\mathbf x)g(s,\mathbf y)
\frac{d^4x\,d^4y}{4\pi^2(|\mathbf x-\mathbf y|^2-(s-t)^2)}>0,$$
because both test functions are nonnegative and nonzero and the denominator
is positive on the support product. More explicitly,
$\langle K_0f,K_0g\rangle_2\ge
(\int f)(\int g)/[4\pi^2(D+r_1+r_2)^2]>0$, since
$|\mathbf x-\mathbf y|^2-(t-s)^2\le(D+r_1+r_2)^2$ there. The zero one-point
values follow from [F1]; commutation follows from [F2] and separation in
step 1.1.
